question.problem:
The **exact** value of $c$ such that the average value of $f(x)=9\sqrt{x}+2$ on the interval $[0,c]$ is equal to $11$ is

$c=$
{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
To solve for $c,$ we apply the average value formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\ 11 & =\frac{1}{c-0}{\int }_{0}^{c}(9\sqrt{x}+2)\,\text{d}x \\ 11 & ={\frac{1}{c}(6{x}^{3/2}+2x)|}_{0}^{c} \\ 11 & =\frac{1}{c}[(6{c}^{3/2}+2c)-0] \\ 11 & =6\sqrt{c}+2 \\ 9 & =6\sqrt{c} \\ \frac{3}{2} & =\sqrt{c} \\ c & =\frac{9}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the value of $c$ is 

$$
c=\frac{9}{4}.
$$
